# Task: Rebuild App.vue showcase using shadcn components ## Description ## Overview ## Goal Replace the hand-crafted card layout in `src/App.vue` with shadcn `Card`, `Button`, and `Badge` components so the starter actually demonstrates the installed stack. ## Current state (verified) `src/App.vue` builds a card manually using raw Tailwind classes (lines 4-67). `WelcomeCard.vue` exists in `src/components/WelcomeCard.vue` but is never imported in App.vue. ## What to change ### Replace manual card with shadcn Card Import from `@/components/ui/card`: ```vue import { Card, CardHeader, CardContent, CardFooter } from '@/components/ui/card' ``` Wrap the existing content sections using these components instead of hand-written `div.bg-card.border.border-border.rounded-lg`. ### Replace the anchor tag CTA with shadcn Button Import `Button` from `@/components/ui/button`: ```vue import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button' ``` Replace the `` tag styled with `class="inline-flex items-center px-6 py-3 bg-primary..."` with ``. ### Add a Badge to each feature item Import `Badge` from `@/components/ui/badge` and add a badge variant (e.g. `variant="secondary"`) next to the feature title in the `v-for` list. ### Use WelcomeCard in a secondary section Add a second section below the main card demonstrating `WelcomeCard` usage: ```vue import WelcomeCard from '@/components/WelcomeCard.vue' ``` Render it with `title="Component Example"` and a default slot containing a short code snippet or description. ## Acceptance criteria - `App.vue` imports and uses at least `Card`, `Button`, and `WelcomeCard` - `npm run build` succeeds - `npm test` passes — update `App.test.ts` to reflect any text or structure changes (e.g. if the h1 text changes, update the test assertion) - Dark mode still works: the dark mode toggle must still function after the refactor - Accessibility is preserved: `id="main-content"` on `
`, `aria-pressed` and `aria-label` on the toggle button ## Context - **Category:** feature - **Priority Score:** 8/10 - **Estimated Complexity:** low ## Reasoning The current App.vue duplicates styling that shadcn components provide. Using the installed components turns this into a live demonstration of the stack, which is the primary purpose of a starter template. WelcomeCard.vue (verified at src/components/WelcomeCard.vue) is already built and tested but is orphaned — this task connects it. ## Category: feature ## Context - Product: Vue 3 + Tailwind + shadcn Starter - Purpose: Modern UI with Vue 3, Tailwind CSS, shadcn-vue, TypeScript, and Vite - Allowed domains: github.com, api.github.com, registry.npmjs.org, cdn.jsdelivr.net ## Deployment - Type: static site — nginx serves files from the `dist/` directory - IMPORTANT: All build output MUST go in the `dist/` directory — nginx will not serve files from any other location - Build: `npm install && npm run build` - Deploy: auto-deploys when PR is merged to main ## Available API Hubs You have access to 2 RSI Platform API Hub(s): AI Hub, Maps Hub. Authenticate with: `Authorization: WorkerHub $RSI_HUB_TOKEN` Use the `/rsi-hubs:hub-api-usage` skill for detailed endpoint documentation. ## Forbidden Actions - No destructive operations on production data - NEVER run 'git init' — the repository is already initialized. Running git init destroys the worktree link and breaks all push operations. - NEVER use 'git push --force' or 'git push --force-with-lease' to any branch. Force pushes destroy other workers' commits. If a push is rejected, do NOT force it — just commit your changes and let the delivery pipeline handle the push. - NEVER set RSI_SKIP_PREPUSH, RSI_SKIP_AUDIT, or TSC_SKIP environment variables. These bypass safety checks and are reserved for human operators only. - NEVER run 'git pull --rebase' or 'git merge' on the base branch. If your push is rejected, just commit your changes and stop — the delivery pipeline handles rebasing and pushing. - NEVER push directly to the base branch (main/master/dev). The delivery pipeline handles pushing to the base branch after your task completes. Only push to your worker branch. ## Product Learning Context (from past tasks) ### Active Recurring Issues - **"spawn gh ENOENT..."** (seen 5x, unresolved) ## Instructions 1. Analyze the task requirements 2. Implement the necessary code changes 3. Ensure the code is clean and follows project conventions 4. Test your changes if possible 5. Commit your changes with a clear, descriptive message ## Before Committing Changes Before creating any git commit, you MUST validate your changes: 1. **TypeScript projects**: If `tsconfig.json` exists in the project root, run `npx tsc --noEmit` to check for type errors. Fix any errors before committing. 2. **Projects with a build script**: If `package.json` has a `build` script, run `npm run build` to verify the build succeeds. Fix any build errors. 3. Only commit when all checks pass. If you encounter pre-existing errors unrelated to your changes, note them in your result summary but do not block your commit over them. ## Tech Stack Changes If your task involves switching the project's tech stack (e.g., Node.js→Python, Vue→vanilla JS, etc.), you MUST update the platform's health probes and build configuration via the Product API. Use the `/rsi-product-api:product-self-service` skill for endpoint details. ## Requesting Human Input If you need human clarification before proceeding (e.g., design decisions, ambiguous requirements, choosing between approaches), create a file `.rsi-needs-input.json` in the project root with: ```json { "questions": [{ "question": "Should the layout use cards or a table?", "options": ["Card layout", "Table layout"], "context": "The current page uses cards but tables would show more data" }] } ``` Then STOP immediately — do not make any code changes. The task will pause and resume with the human's answer injected into the prompt. Only use this when you genuinely cannot proceed without clarification. Do NOT use it for trivial decisions you can make yourself. ## Follow-Up Tasks (Optional) If you discover something important during implementation that should NOT be fixed in this PR (different concern, separate scope), you may output a follow-up tasks section. Most tasks should NOT need this — only use it for genuinely important discoveries. ```follow-up-tasks [ { "title": "Brief title of the follow-up", "description": "What needs to be done and why", "type": "code", "priority": 7, "reason": "Why this can't be addressed in the current PR", "category": "bugfix" } ] ```
